title: Been publishing free daily stock lists with full trade plans for months - curious how others would use something like this
author: One-Cellist-8159
selftext:
One thing I kept running into was having decent research ideas but still spending way too long every morning turning them into actual trade plans with a clear entry, stop, and realistic targets. Screening tools and news give you names, but the “okay, where do I actually get in, where’s the invalidation, and what’s the risk/reward?” part was still on me.

So I’ve been using (and publicly publishing on) an AI research terminal where different agents work together and produce structured trade plans. Every day before the open I hand-pick and publish a short curated list - usually somewhere between 10 and 30 stocks. I’ve been doing this for months now. Some names keep showing up, which builds a bit more confidence for me, and a decent number of them have moved well in the following days to weeks on plain stocks (no options needed).

It’s completely free to access - just log in with Google. You can check the day’s list in the morning, look at the AI-generated plans, and adjust anything you want (levels, sizing, etc.). There’s also an AI report button that lets you download a CSV of the trade plans for the whole published list if you want to track them offline later.

If you’re newer or just testing it, the easiest approach is probably to just watch how the names behave over the next few days or weeks before doing anything. Desktop is preferred, but it works fine on mobile and shows the same information.

Curious if anyone else here has found a good way to combine AI-generated plans with their own filters and experience, or if you’ve tried anything similar. Feedback is welcome - there’s a contact form for feature requests, bugs, or general questions: [https://edgecipher.ai/contact](https://edgecipher.ai/contact)  
  
Terminal link: [https://edgecipher.ai/terminal](https://edgecipher.ai/terminal)

Let me know if i can improve experience in anyway or any inconsistencies you guys see.

Not financial advice. Past movement doesn’t guarantee anything. This is just one tool, and the decision (and risk management) stays with you.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: what I'd want before using a list like this is the old plans graded after the fact: how many hit the stop before the first target, on the real bars, not the ones people remember. I built Quantradin partly to do that grading, on paper, for US stocks, without peeking ahead. quantradin.com, nothing on it is real money.
